Kweichow Moutai shifts i Moutai from flash sales to daily sales
sum: China’s top baijiu producer is trying to match shipments to weaker demand, curbing inventory buildup in distribution channels

Kweichow Moutai is reshaping how it sells its flagship baijiu as weak consumer demand continues to pressure China’s liquor market, telling investors on Tuesday, Nov. 10, that its i Moutai digital platform will gradually move away from flash sales and toward regular daily sales, while the company also said it did not add new base-liquor capacity for the 2027 production cycle after a market review.

The changes, outlined by Wang Li, a company director who is performing the general manager’s duties, mark a broader push by China’s biggest premium baijiu producer to align shipments more closely with real consumer demand and reduce reliance on the old practice of pushing inventory into distribution channels.

i Moutai, the company’s self-operated e-commerce platform, went online on March 31, 2022. According to Kweichow Moutai’s third-quarter report, the platform generated 58.562 billion yuan in liquor revenue excluding tax in the first nine months of 2026, equal to about 43.9% of the company’s total operating revenue of 133.284 billion yuan. That has made the platform one of the most important sales channels in the Moutai system.

Wang said the platform’s next stage has three parts: moving from the current rush-purchase model to one aimed at meeting everyday consumer demand, serving as the debut platform for new products and becoming a service hub that works with offline stores to improve customer service.

On Wednesday, Nov. 11, 16 Moutai products, including premium and aged editions, began using an all-day dynamic replenishment model on the platform, while other products kept the previous release method. The shift follows a year in which the company steadily increased supply through i Moutai.

At the start of 2026, Kweichow Moutai began a market-oriented overhaul centered on consumers. The company expanded the range of products sold on i Moutai and opened self-operated stores to public sales. It also moved away from the long-used system of forcing stock into channels ahead of demand.

Wuliangye stock hit by 48.25% third-quarter profit drop
sum: Wuliangye reported a sharp third-quarter setback on October 28 as weaker demand and lower sales volumes weighed on its baijiu business. According to Vinetur, revenue for the three months ended September 30 fell 37.68 percent year over year to 4.44 billion yuan. Net profit attributable to shareholders dropped 48.25 percent to 957.7 million yuan.

The quarterly decline contrasted with stronger cumulative results. Revenue for the first nine months rose 7.25 percent to 32.86 billion yuan, while net profit attributable to shareholders increased 49.98 percent to 9.71 billion yuan. Profit excluding non-recurring items advanced 46.18 percent to 9.44 billion yuan.

Wuliangye attributed the stronger nine-month performance partly to a low profit base in the prior-year period and effective sales measures during the Lunar New Year selling season. Core products recorded solid sales during that period, offsetting the weaker third quarter.

The report also pointed to pressure in cash conversion and distribution. Operating cash flow for the first nine months fell 99.83 percent year over year to 46.7 million yuan. Inventory rose to 24.20 billion yuan from 20.07 billion yuan at the end of the previous year, while contract liabilities fell to 8.93 billion yuan from 13.46 billion yuan.

Wuliangye produces baijiu, a Chinese distilled spirit, with products including the Wuliangye flagship brand and Wuliangye 1618. The company is based in China and operates in the premium baijiu market, where Vinetur describes it as one of the country's largest producers.

Its business is concentrated in branded spirits and related sales channels rather than a diversified consumer portfolio. The company remains a major specialist in premium Chinese liquor, while the broader category includes competitors such as Kweichow Moutai, Luzhou Laojiao and Shanxi Fenjiu.

Investors are likely to focus next on whether Wuliangye can reduce channel inventories, stabilize demand and convert reported profit growth into stronger operating cash flow. The Shanghai Composite provides the relevant broader-market context for this China-based company: Current market reports.

items.t: Unitree Stock Extends Rebound, Briefly Touching 809 Yuan
sum: Gasgoo Munich- On November 10, Unitree Tech (688836) opened strong and kept climbing, briefly touching 809 yuan during intraday trading. The stock surged back above the 800-yuan mark, pushing its total market capitalization past 320 billion yuan at one point.
By the closing bell, Unitree’s gains had narrowed to roughly 6.3%. The stock settled at 761.01 yuan, leaving its market capitalization at around 307.8 billion yuan.

By the morning session, Unitree had overtaken former "stock king" Semight Instruments to become the third-priciest stock on the A-share market, trailing only Kweichow Moutai and Cambricon. Its market valuation also eclipsed traditional blue chips such as China Pacific Insurance, East Money, and Wuliangye.

Cast back to August 19: Unitree debuted on the STAR Market at an issue price of 150.80 yuan. It opened at 1,100 yuan on day one, briefly sending its market cap above 440 billion yuan. But the rally didn't last. By early September, the stock had halved from its peak. It hit a post-listing low of 404.03 yuan on October 15—a roughly 63% retreat from the highs.

Just 18 trading days later, Unitree has clawed its way back to 800 yuan—nearly doubling its value. The momentum behind this rebound stems from two sources: sector-wide strength and external validation.

On the sector front, humanoid robot concepts rallied across the board. Tongxing Tech surged by the 20% daily limit, while Guangyang, Fulai New Material, and Yijia He also hit limit-up levels. Leaders and supply chain players rose in tandem.

On the news front, Apple’s research team published a paper on arXiv on November 4 detailing HALO, an autonomous control system for humanoid robots. The team open-sourced its data, models, and deployment code—using Unitree’s G1 as the verification platform. The robot completed 360 individual tests across six unseen, unmapped real-world environments with an average success rate of 91%, effectively cementing the G1 as a reference standard for humanoid research.

items.t: Italy Dominates U.S. Organic Wine Imports With a 51% Share
sum: The report said imports reached €35.6 million in 2025, then rose +2.2% in the first eight months of 2026

Italy is the leading foreign supplier of organic wine in the United States, according to a new 2026 market focus from Ita.Bio, an initiative backed by Italy’s trade agency ICE with support from FederBio and research by Nomisma.

The study said the United States imported €35.6 million worth of Italian organic wine in 2025. In the first eight months of 2026, the value of those imports rose +2.2% from the same period in 2025. Italy held a 51% share by value of U.S. organic wine imports, well ahead of other supplier countries, the report said.

The findings come as the broader U.S. organic market continues to expand. Nomisma said U.S. sales of organic products reached €60.4 billion, up +105.8% from 2014. It also said 54% of Americans buy organic products at least once a week, showing that organic goods have moved into regular household consumption.

The report pointed to a strong opening for Italian exporters beyond wine. In a survey of 1,000 household food purchasing decision-makers ages 18 to 65 in New York and California, 43% said they had bought an Italian-made organic food product at least once in the previous year. Italy also ranked first for perceived quality and safety in organic products, with 56% of respondents placing it ahead of countries including France and Canada.

Italian organic wine appears to be benefiting from that wider reputation at a time when the U.S. wine market is changing. The study said total wine consumption in the United States fell to 31 million hectoliters in 2025, down 10% from 2019. At the same time, it said consumer interest is rising for products seen as innovative, healthier or lower in alcohol, which may be helping support demand for organic labels.

Even with Italy’s lead, the report said several barriers are still limiting growth. Among organic consumers who do not buy Italian organic products, 40% said prices were too high, 37% said the products were not easy to find in their usual shopping channels, and 30% said they had trouble recognizing them on store shelves or in restaurants.

Chinese stocks rebound as investors bet on AI applications, policy support: analyst
sum: Chinese mainland markets staged a technical rebound on Monday after a bleak end to last week, with growth and innovation shares leading gains as investors rotated into artificial intelligence (AI) applications and bet on fresh policy support for the capital markets, according to a market analyst.

The Shanghai Composite Index was up more than once percent, while the STAR 50 jumped 3.1 percent and the ChiNext gained 1.9 percent. The CSI 300 rose a more modest 0.8 percent, offering some relief after a record 12 consecutive weekly declines.
Timothy Pope, a market analyst at China Global Television Network (CGTN), said the session's standout theme was a shift toward companies involved in the commercial application of AI.

"Today we saw investors chasing companies involved in the commercial application of AI, rather than the nuts and bolts of it, semiconductors and the like. So, there was a lot of interest in companies linked to AI-generated short video dramas, animations as well, with Mango Excellent Media hitting its 20 percent daily upward limit. Aside from that, we had liquor producers and brokerages also doing well today. Kweichow Moutai gained more than three percent. Guotai Haitong Securities climbed more than two percent. And we saw two, at least two, other brokerage listings hitting their 10 percent daily limit today," he said.
The analyst attributed much of the optimism to rising hopes for policy support.

"A lot of this seems to have come from rising hopes of policy support. We saw China's manufacturing and non-manufacturing PMI results come out at the weekend, and both had slipped into contraction territory. And [on] Friday, after the Shanghai Composite Index closed below 3,600 points, since then, there's been more speculation about additional state support for the capital markets, too. Reports that financial regulators were meeting to discuss measures to support share buybacks helped lift brokerage stocks in particular," said Pope.

As golf sees resurgence in Singapore, more should be done to make the sport accessible and affordable
sum: There are many young and talented players here who need the opportunity and space to hone their skills
THE successful conclusion of this year’s Singapore Open golf tournament on Sunday (Apr 26) should be cause for cheer within the local golfing community.

Over the last 15 years or so, the marquee event – which used to be held annually and was backed by the likes of Barclays and SMBC, and most recently, Kweichow Moutai in 2025 – saw some editions scrapped due to the lack of a title sponsor. The 2021 competition did not take place because of the Covid-19 pandemic.

Decades ago, Singapore’s Laguna National Golf Resort Club hosted a series of Singapore Masters events. These attracted top players from around the world like Phil Mickelson, Padraig Harrington, Rory McIlroy, Sergio Garcia, Adam Scott and Angel Cabrera to Singapore.

The top rated players at this year’s Singapore Open, with The Business Times as the presenting partner for the first time, were lesser known names like the eventual champion South Korea’s Ham Jeong-woo, Thailand’s Ekpharit Wu, India’s Gaganjeet Bhullar and Australian Travis Smyth.

It is encouraging that the national Open was revived last year after a three-year absence. But the big question is whether the event will be sustainable and can continue to take place uninterrupted from now on.
This issue is particularly pertinent given the state of golf in Singapore today.

sum: As Dry January encourages millions to rethink their relationship with alcohol, the global drinks industry continues to evolve far beyond traditional consumption habits.
What began as a month-long pause has become a wider movement driving demand for moderation, premium quality and no-alcohol alternatives.
From iconic beers and ciders to world-leading spirits, champagnes and baijiu, the biggest beverage companies are expanding portfolios to meet changing tastes and occasions.
These industry giants balance heritage with innovation, investing in sustainability, responsible drinking and new product formats.
Food & Drink Digital has ranked the top 10 most influential alcoholic beverage companies shaping the future of the sector worldwide.
The Carlsberg Group is a global brewer with a broad portfolio spanning hundreds of beers, ciders and no-alcohol options across multiple markets.

Its range combines international flagships such as Carlsberg and 1664 with strong local brands, seasonal specials and innovation-led formats including radlers, flavoured wheat beers and alcohol-free variants.

items.t: Spirits rise as baijiu shares rally on Lunar New Year demand
sum: With liquor stocks viewed as a barometer of real estate-linked business activity, the rally reflects renewed hopes for the property sector
Chinese liquor stocks jumped on Thursday ahead of Lunar New Year, with retailers reportedly building inventories of spirits typically consumed at family reunions and corporate banquets.

Shares of Kweichow Moutai – China’s best-known baijiu maker and the most valuable stock on the mainland market – climbed more than 9 per cent in afternoon trading to 1,445 yuan, their highest level in over a month.
The stock closed the session 8.6 per cent higher at 1,437.72 yuan.
